definition_zh: 冒险；奇遇；冒险精神；大胆的尝试
definition_en: an unusual and exciting experience, the willingness to take risks, or a bold new enterprise
core_image: 一张摊开的地图，边角画着还没走过的海岸线
scene: 他们辞了工作，开着一辆旧车往西走，没有计划。 Their trip across the desert turned into a real adventure.
sceneCN: 这里的 adventure 是「冒险经历」（第 1 个义项：不寻常而刺激的经历）；句意是他们穿越沙漠的旅行变成了一场真正的冒险。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险；奇遇；冒险精神；大胆尝试

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「爱冒险的；惊险的」
由名词加表人后缀构成，义为「冒险家」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「爱冒险地」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「不幸的遭遇；意外事故」

senses.title: An exciting and unusual experience
senses.definition: an unusual, exciting and possibly risky experience or journey
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常、令人兴奋且可能带风险的经历或旅程
senses.example: The climb was the adventure of a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攀登是一生只有一次的冒险。
senses.why: Latin adventurus means about to happen, from advenire, to come to; an adventure is whatever is coming towards you, unknown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adventurus 意为「即将发生」，出自 advenire（来临）；adventure 就是那件正朝你走来、尚不可知的事。

senses.title: A willingness to take risks
senses.definition: the quality of being eager to try new or risky things
senses.definitionCN: 乐于尝试新鲜或冒险之事的性格
senses.example: She has a real sense of adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 她真有冒险精神。
senses.why: The events gave their name to the appetite for them, so the noun can mean the spirit rather than the trip.
senses.whyCN: 这类事件把自己的名字给了对它的渴望，于是名词可以指精神而非旅程。

senses.title: A bold and risky enterprise
senses.definition: a new project or business venture that involves considerable risk
senses.definitionCN: 涉及相当风险的新项目或商业尝试
senses.example: Starting the company was a costly adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 创办这家公司是一次代价高昂的冒险。
senses.why: Business likes the word for its hint of the unknown: a new firm is a journey with no map.
senses.whyCN: 商业喜欢这个词所带的「未知」意味：一家新公司就是一次没有地图的旅程。

intro.en: What is about to happen, and therefore uncertain.
intro.cn: 「即将发生之事」，因而也是不确定之事。

items.en: venire meant to come, and underlies invent, prevent and convene.
items.cn: venire 意为来，invent、prevent 与 convene 都出自它。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus venire formed advenire, to come to, to arrive.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 venire 构成 advenire，意为「来到、抵达」。

items.en: adventura meant the things that are about to happen, often used of chance or fate.
items.cn: adventura 指「即将发生的事」，常用于机遇或命运。

items.en: Old French aventure named a knight's chance encounter and the tale told about it.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 指骑士的偶然遭遇，以及围绕它讲的故事。

items.en: English adopted adventure for risky journeys, then for the spirit that seeks them.
items.cn: 英语借入 adventure 指有风险的旅程，后又指追寻它的那股精神。

note.en: The first group is the coming root; the second gathers words for risky journeys and ventures.
note.cn: 第一组是表示「来」的词根；第二组收有风险的旅程与事业。

a person who seeks adventure
an unlucky accident
an organized journey for a purpose
a daring and slightly reckless act

normalIntro.en: venire, to come, sits inside the middle of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 意为「来」的 venire，就藏在词的中间。

normal.en: adventure began as the things that are about to come to you.
normal.cn: adventure 最初指「即将来到你面前的事」。

normal.en: a sense of adventure names the appetite, not the event.
normal.cn: a sense of adventure 指那股渴望，而不是事件本身。

normal.en: adventurous is the adjective, adventurer the person.
normal.cn: adventurous 是形容词，adventurer 是那个人。

normal.en: misadventure adds mis- and means an unlucky accident.
normal.cn: 加 mis- 得到 misadventure，指不幸的意外。

normal.en: The ending -ture marks nouns, as in nature and picture.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ture 标记名词，如 nature 与 picture。

abstract.en: See a map with a blank coast at the edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，边角是一片空白的海岸。

abstract.en: Picture an old car packed and pointed west.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆装满行李、朝西开的旧车。

abstract.en: Think of a door opening onto a road you have never taken.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门通向从没走过的那条路。

examples.en: The climb was the adventure of a lifetime.
examples.cn: 那次攀登是一生只有一次的冒险。

examples.en: She has a real sense of adventure.
examples.cn: 她真有冒险精神。

examples.en: Starting the company was a costly adventure.
examples.cn: 创办这家公司是一次代价高昂的冒险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的文彻」——额头上写着文彻的名字，因为他总说走就走，地图都不带。

root: 拉丁语 adventura（即将来临之事），出自 advenire（来到），由 ad-（向）与 venire（来）构成；本义「未知的将来」，后指冒险经历与冒险精神。

sensesIntro.en: What is coming towards you can be a journey, an appetite or a gamble.
sensesIntro.cn: 朝你走来的东西，可以是一段旅程、一种渴望，也可以是一场赌注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map with one blank coast.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上有一段空白海岸。

branches.en: a climb remembered for years
branches.cn: 多年后仍被记起的攀登

branches.en: a road trip without a plan
branches.cn: 没有计划的公路旅行

branches.en: a traveller who never says no
branches.cn: 从不说「不」的旅行者

branches.en: a company launched on savings
branches.cn: 用积蓄创办的公司

branches.en: a journey and a business alike unmapped
branches.cn: 旅程与生意同样没有地图

intro.cn: 方向词头加在表示「来」的词根上。

latinIntro.en: venire also gives invent, prevent and avenue.
latinIntro.cn: venire 也给出 invent、prevent 与 avenue。

definition_en: something you allow in order to end an argument, or a special right given to someone
core_image: 守门人把栏杆抬起一半，让对方先过去
scene: 谈判桌上，双方各自放下一个条件。 Each side made a concession before the deal was signed.
sceneCN: 这里 concession 指「让步」（第 1 个义项：为达成协议而让出的一点）；句意是签约前每一方都作了一项让步。

derivatives.zh: 承认；让步
让步的
优惠的；让步的
特许的；优惠的

senses.title: A give in an argument
senses.definition: something you agree to give up in order to reach agreement
senses.definitionCN: 为达成协议而同意放弃的东西
senses.example: The union won a small concession on pay.
senses.exampleCN: 工会争取到了薪酬上的一点让步。
senses.why: One side lifts the barrier a little so the other can move.
senses.whyCN: 一方把栏杆抬起一点，好让另一方通过。

senses.title: A special right
senses.definition: the right to sell or use something, often given by a government
senses.definitionCN: 通常由政府授予的销售或使用某物的权利
senses.example: The company holds the mining concession.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司持有采矿特许权。
senses.why: A right granted is also a kind of thing yielded by the stronger side.
senses.whyCN: 被授予的权利，也是强者让出的一种东西。

senses.title: A lower price
senses.definition: a reduced price for students, children or old people
senses.definitionCN: 为学生、儿童或老人提供的减价
senses.example: Students get a concession on tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 学生买票可以享受优惠。
senses.why: The full price is lowered, as if part of the cost were given away.
senses.whyCN: 全价被降低，就像把部分费用让了出去。

intro.en: Concession comes from Latin concessio, a granting, from concedere, to give way or allow.
intro.cn: concession 来自拉丁语 concessio（准许），源自动词 concedere（让路、允许）。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or to yield ground.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出地盘。

items.en: Concedere meant to allow or to grant a request.
items.cn: concedere 意为允许或应允请求。

items.en: Concessio named the act of granting something.
items.cn: concessio 指给予某物的行为。

items.en: Old French concession kept the legal sense of a granted right.
items.cn: 古法语 concession 保留了授予权利的法律含义。

items.en: English concession first meant a thing granted or allowed.
items.cn: 英语 concession 最初指被授予或允许的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to concession, and the meaning group names other words for yielding or privilege.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concession 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示让出与特权的词。

entries.definition: offered at a reduced price
a line of people moving in order
a statement that you have done wrong
a deal in which each side gives up something
an amount that is permitted
a special right given to a person or group

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a barrier lifted halfway, then move to granted rights and to cheaper tickets.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从抬到一半的栏杆开始，再走到授予的权利与更便宜的票。

normal.en: Concession is the noun of concede, so it is the thing you let go.
normal.cn: concession 是 concede 的名词，所以它就是被你放手的东西。

normal.en: A concession stand sells snacks inside the barrier.
normal.cn: concession stand 就是在栏杆内卖零食的小摊。

normal.en: A mining concession is a right dug out of the ground.
normal.cn: 采矿特许权是从地里挖出来的一项权利。

normal.en: A student concession is a price that steps back for you.
normal.cn: 学生优惠是一张为你后退的价格。

normal.en: Concessive clauses begin with words like although, which also give way.
normal.cn: 让步从句以 although 这类词开头，它们也在让出立场。

abstract.en: Picture a gatekeeper lifting the bar just enough for one person.
abstract.cn: 想象守门人把栏杆抬到刚够一个人通过。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding a signed permit across a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把签好的许可证推过桌面。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket stamped a little cheaper.
abstract.cn: 想象一张票被盖上便宜一些的章。

examples.en: The offer included several concessions on working hours.
examples.cn: 这份提议在工作时间上包含了几项让步。

examples.en: The firm won the oil concession for twenty years.
examples.cn: 这家公司赢得了二十年的石油开采特许权。

examples.en: Children over six must pay the full fare, without concession.
examples.cn: 六岁以上儿童须付全价，没有优惠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 concession 记成 con（一起）加 cess（走）加 ion：从自己的立场上走出去一步，就是让步。

root: 源自拉丁语 concedere（com 一起 + cedere 走、让）的名词 concessio，本义是让路、准许，后指让步、特许权与优惠。

sensesIntro.en: From a small step back in an argument, to a right granted, and finally to a price lowered.
sensesIntro.cn: 从争论中后退一小步，到被授予的权利，最后到被降低的价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gatekeeper raising the bar halfway so the other side can pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：守门人把栏杆抬起一半，让对方先过去。

branches.en: A give in an argument is the common everyday sense.
branches.cn: 争论中的让步是常见的日常义项。

branches.en: A granted right turns the give into a legal object.
branches.cn: 被授予的权利把让步变成法律对象。

branches.en: A cheaper ticket is a concession in money.
branches.cn: 更便宜的票是金钱上的让步。

branches.en: Both senses describe something handed over by the stronger side.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述强者交出的东西。

branches.en: A right and a discount are both special treatment.
branches.cn: 权利与折扣都是特殊待遇。

intro.en: Concession is built on Latin com-, together, plus cedere, to go, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: concession 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、cedere（走）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin go base cess- also gives process, access and recession.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的行走词基 cess- 还给出 process、access 与 recession。

items.example: He conceded the point at once.
The bank offered a concessional loan.
items.exampleCN: 银行提供了一笔优惠贷款。

items.example: They run a concessionary fare scheme.
items.exampleCN: 他们实施优惠票价方案。

items.meaning: a person who holds a concession

items.exampleCN: 特许经营者经营公园咖啡馆。

items.meaning: a line of people moving forward
items.example: A procession moved slowly up the hill.

definition_zh: 部分的；不完全的；偏袒的；偏爱的
definition_en: covering only a part of something and not the whole, favouring one person or side unfairly, or, in the phrase be partial to, liking something very much
core_image: 一面墙只刷了一半，另一半还留着旧漆的颜色
scene: 画廊的墙上挂着一幅被烟熏过的旧画，右半边颜色已经褪去。 The restorer could only see a partial view of the original painting.
sceneCN: 这里的 partial 是「部分的、不完全的」（第 1 个义项：只涉及整体的一部分）；句意为修复师只能看到原画的一个局部。图中可辨识物件：旧画、熏痕、褪色的半边。

pos.zh: 部分的；不完全的；偏袒的；偏爱的

derivatives.zh: 由 partial 加 -ly 构成，义为「部分地；不完全地」
由 partial 加 -ity 构成，义为「偏袒；偏爱」
由否定前缀 im- 加 partial 构成，义为「不偏不倚的；公正的」

senses.title: Covering only a part
senses.definition: covering or affecting only a part of something, not the whole
senses.definitionCN: 只覆盖或影响某物的一部分，而不是整体
senses.example: The restorer could only see a partial view of the original painting.
senses.exampleCN: 修复师只能看到原画的一个局部。
senses.why: Partial is an adjective built on part, so it describes whatever holds only some of a whole, and the missing remainder is felt in the word itself.
senses.whyCN: partial 是建立在 part 之上的形容词，所以它描述只占整体一部分的东西，词里本身就带着「还缺一部分」的感觉。

senses.title: Favouring one side unfairly
senses.definition: supporting one person, group or side more than another, especially in a way that is unfair
senses.definitionCN: 对人、群体或一方给予更多支持，尤指以不公平的方式
senses.example: The referee was accused of being partial to the home team.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判被指责偏袒主队。
senses.why: If you take only one part of a dispute, you no longer stand above the whole; the word for a part becomes the word for taking sides.
senses.whyCN: 在一场争执里只取其中一部分，人就不再站在整体的上方；于是「部分」这个词变成了「站到一边」的意思。

senses.title: Fond of something
senses.definition: liking a thing or a person very much, used in the phrase be partial to
senses.definitionCN: 非常喜欢某物或某人，用于 be partial to 这一说法
senses.example: She is partial to strong coffee in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她早上偏爱浓咖啡。
senses.why: Liking something is a mild form of favouring it, so the same adjective moves from courts and referees to the breakfast table without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 喜欢某样东西，是「偏向」的温和形式，于是同一个形容词从法庭与球场走到了早餐桌上，形状丝毫未变。

intro.en: Partial comes from Latin partialis, an adjective from pars, part; French passed it to English as parcial, where it first meant belonging to a part and later meant favouring one side.
intro.cn: partial 来自拉丁语 partialis，是 pars（部分）派生的形容词；法语把它写作 parcial 传给英语，先指「属于某一部分的」，后指「偏向一方的」。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and its adjective partialis described whatever belonged to only one part.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，其形容词 partialis 描述只属于某一部分的东西。

items.en: Partialis named what is divided or one-sided, and it could already describe a person who takes a side.
items.cn: partialis 指被分开的或偏向一边的，已经能形容站到某一边的人。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parcial, meaning belonging to a part or showing favour to one side.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 parcial，意为属于一部分的，或对一方表示偏袒的。

items.en: Middle English partial kept both the idea of an incomplete whole and the idea of an unfair preference.
items.cn: 中古英语的 partial 同时保留「整体不完整」与「偏好不公平」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English adds the polite phrase be partial to for liking something, and pairs partial with impartial for fair judgement.
items.cn: 现代英语添上表示喜欢的客气说法 be partial to，又用 impartial 与 partial 相对，表示公正的判断。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the part family side by side so the split between partial, partly and particular is clear; the near-meaning group gathers words for incomplete and for biased.
note.cn: 形近组把 part 一族并排摆开，好让 partial、partly 与 particular 的分叉一目了然；近义组收表示「不完整」与「有偏向」的词。

entries.definition: In some measure but not completely; the adverb built directly on part.
entries.definitionCN: 在某种程度上但不完全；直接由 part 构成的副词。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; from the small form of Latin pars.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；出自拉丁语 pars 的小称。

entries.definition: One specific item or quality rather than any other; from the same small form of pars.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的某一项或某种性质；出自同一小称词。

entries.definition: A wrapped package or a plot of land, also from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 包裹或一块地，同样出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: Not finished or not having all its parts.
entries.definitionCN: 未完成的，或缺少某些部分的。

entries.definition: Unfairly favouring one side over another.
Showing only one point of view, or unfair to one party.
entries.definitionCN: 只呈现一种看法的，或对一方不公的。

entries.definition: Giving an advantage to one person or group.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人或某群体优待的。

normalIntro.en: Partial keeps the shape of part plus a Latin adjective ending, so its hooks show how a piece of a whole turns into a biased choice and then into a quiet liking.
normalIntro.cn: partial 保留着 part 加拉丁形容词词尾的形状，记忆钩子展示「整体的一块」如何变成「偏向的选择」，再变成「含蓄的喜欢」。

normal.en: Partial is part with an adjective ending, so it always suggests that a remainder is missing.
normal.cn: partial 就是 part 加形容词词尾，所以它总暗示还差着一部分。

normal.en: Partly is the adverb for the same idea, while partial is the adjective; a partial success is the thing, and the plan partly worked is the action.
normal.cn: partly 是同一想法的副词，partial 是形容词；partial success 说的是那件事，the plan partly worked 说的是进展。

normal.en: Particular comes from the same small piece of Latin but points to one identified item, not to a fraction of it.
normal.cn: particular 出自同一个「小块」，但指的是一件被认定的东西，而不是它的一部分。

normal.en: Impartial adds the negative prefix im-, so an impartial judge has no part in the argument at all.
normal.cn: impartial 加上否定前缀 im-，所以公正的法官在争执中不属于任何一边。

normal.en: Be partial to is a gentle way of saying you like something, as if you were admitting a small preference.
normal.cn: be partial to 是说自己喜欢某物的委婉方式，像是在承认一点小小的偏好。

abstract.en: A word that means both incomplete and unfair hints that taking a part is already a kind of taking sides.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示「不完整」与「不公平」，暗示「取一部分」本身就是一种「站边」。

abstract.en: Because partial can describe a view, a payment and a referee, the language treats love, money and judgement as the same act of dividing.
abstract.cn: 既然 partial 能形容视野、付款与裁判，语言就把爱、钱与判断都看成同一种「分割」的动作。

abstract.en: The opposite of partial is impartial rather than whole, which suggests that fairness is imagined as owning no share.
abstract.cn: partial 的对立面是 impartial 而不是 whole，这说明「公正」被想象成「不占任何一份」。

examples.en: The restorer could only see a partial view of the original painting.
examples.cn: 修复师只能看到原画的一个局部。

examples.en: The referee was accused of being partial to the home team.
examples.cn: 裁判被指责偏袒主队。

examples.en: She is partial to strong coffee in the morning.
examples.cn: 她早上偏爱浓咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕输」——裁判怕输球的一方闹起来，哨子就偏了过去；记住 partial 既有「部分的」，也有「偏袒的」。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）派生 partialis（属于一部分的），经古法语 parcial 进入英语；与 partly、particular、particle 同出 part，但 partial 走的是「只占一部分—偏向一边—偏爱」这一路。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a share of a whole; the senses divide into what covers only part, what favours one side, and what quietly prefers one thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是整体中的一份；义项按「只覆盖一部分」「偏向一边」「暗暗偏爱某物」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall painted on one half only, the other half still showing old paint.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙只刷了一半，另一半还留着旧漆的颜色。

branches.en: a canvas seen through smoke, its edges missing
branches.cn: 隔着烟尘看到的一幅画，边缘缺失

branches.en: a debt repaid in two instalments
branches.cn: 分两次还清的一笔欠款

branches.en: a whistle that always favours the home crowd
branches.cn: 总偏向主队看台的哨声

branches.en: a judge who belongs to neither camp
branches.cn: 不属于任何一方的法官

branches.en: a cup of strong coffee kept for oneself
branches.cn: 留给自己的那杯浓咖啡

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective on pars, passed through French, and English adds three endings to build the adverb, the noun and the negative opposite.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在 pars 上的拉丁形容词，经法语传来，英语再加三个词缀，造出副词、名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars and partialis are both recorded, so partial shares a documented ancestry with part, particle, particular and parcel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 与 partialis 均有记录，因此 partial 与 part、particle、particular、parcel 共享有据可查的世系。

items.meaning: belonging to, of the kind of

items.meaningCN: 后缀：构成表性质的名词

definition_zh: 充分地；足够地；合乎要求地
definition_en: in a way that is enough in amount, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose
core_image: 往杯子里倒水，水面刚好停在杯壁那一道刻度线上
scene: 帐篷外的雨越下越大，队长挨个检查每个人的背包。 The team was adequately equipped for the storm.
sceneCN: 这里的 adequately 是「充分地」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度上足够）；句意是队伍为这场暴风雨做了充分的装备。

pos.zh: 副词：充分地；足够地；合乎要求地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 还原为形容词，义为「足够的；适当的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「足够；适当」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不足的；不够格的」
由否定形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「不足；缺陷」

senses.title: Enough in amount
senses.definition: in a quantity or degree large enough to meet a need
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上大到足以满足需要
senses.example: The shelter was adequately stocked with food and water.
senses.exampleCN: 避难所储备了足够的食物和水。
senses.why: adequately is the adverb of adequate, which Latin built from adaequare, to make equal: the supply is made equal to the need.
senses.whyCN: adequately 是 adequate 的副词；拉丁语 adaequare 意为「使相等」，即把供给做到与需要相等。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: to a standard that is acceptable, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 达到可以接受的标准，但算不上出色
senses.example: She answered every question adequately, though without much flair.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个问题都答得合格，只是没什么出彩之处。
senses.why: Once the measure matches the demand, the result only has to cross the line, so the adverb often means acceptable rather than excellent.
senses.whyCN: 只要分量与需求相称，结果就只需过线，所以这个副词常表示「合格」而非「出色」。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of equality, turned into an adverb of sufficiency.
intro.cn: 一个来自拉丁语的「相等」形容词，变成了表示「足够」的副词。

items.en: aequus meant level, even or equal, and gave aequitas, fairness.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、相等的，并生出 aequitas「公平」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus aequare 'to make equal' formed adaequare, to make equal to, to level up.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 aequare（使相等）构成 adaequare，意为「使与……相等、拉平」。

items.en: The participle adaequatus described a thing made proportionate to its measure.
items.cn: 分词 adaequatus 描述的是「被做得与其尺度相称」的事物。

items.en: English borrowed adequate from Latin in the seventeenth century; the adverb adequately followed it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪直接从拉丁语借入 adequate，副词 adequately 随后出现。

items.en: Modern usage marks the line between enough and not enough, and often hints at 'only just enough'.
items.cn: 现代用法划出「够」与「不够」的分界，还常暗示「刚刚够」。

note.en: The first group shares the equality root; the second gathers adverbs of sufficiency with different shades.
note.cn: 第一组共享「相等」词根；第二组是几个表示「足够」的副词，语气各有差别。

entries.definition: enough for the purpose
not enough for the purpose
the state of not being enough
to a degree that is enough
in a way that fits the purpose
to a fair but not high degree

normalIntro.en: Three pieces carry the word: ad-, aequus and -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由三块拼成：ad-、aequus 与 -ly。

normal.en: ad- means to, aequus means equal, so adequately means up to the mark.
normal.cn: ad- 表示「向」，aequus 表示「相等」，adequately 就是「达到刻度」。

normal.en: The adjective ends in -ate and the adverb simply adds -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词以 -ate 结尾，副词直接加 -ly。

normal.en: adequately prepared is the commonest pairing in writing.
normal.cn: adequately prepared（准备充分）是书面语里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Reports like to pair adequately funded with adequately staffed.
normal.cn: 报告里常把 adequately funded 与 adequately staffed 成对使用。

normal.en: Spell it with a single d in the middle: adequate.
normal.cn: 拼写中间只有一个 d：adequate。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler against a cup and the water stopping exactly at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象把尺子贴在杯壁上，水面刚好停在刻度线。

abstract.en: See a scale with the goods on one side and the need on the other, level.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端，一边是货物，一边是需要，正好持平。

abstract.en: Imagine a report card with every box ticked but no stars.
abstract.cn: 想象一张成绩单，每一栏都打了勾，却没有星。

examples.en: The shelter was adequately stocked with food and water.
examples.cn: 避难所储备了足够的食物和水。

examples.en: He was adequately paid for the extra hours.
examples.cn: 他加班的那几个小时得到了足够的报酬。

examples.en: The report adequately explains why the project failed.
examples.cn: 这份报告充分解释了项目失败的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱得夸特利」——他爱夸自己准备得够充分，其实只是刚刚够用。

root: 拉丁语 adaequare（使相等），由 ad-（向）与 aequus（相等的）构成；adequate 本义是「与需要相称的」，加 -ly 成为副词。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb of measurement covers both quantity and quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「量」的副词，既管数量，也管质量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water stopping exactly at the marked line.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面正好停在刻度线上。

branches.en: a tank filled to the required level
branches.cn: 水箱加到规定水位

branches.en: an answer that is correct but plain
branches.cn: 正确但平淡的回答

branches.en: supply matched to demand
branches.cn: 供给与需求相称

branches.en: work that clears the bar without shining
branches.cn: 过线却不出彩的工作

branches.en: the same line seen as quantity and as quality
branches.cn: 同一条线，从数量与质量两个方向看

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a root of equality and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示方向的词头、一个表示相等的词根、一个副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: aequus also gives equilibrium and equator.
latinIntro.cn: aequus 也给出 equilibrium 与 equator。

definition_en: rough to touch, made of large particles, or rude and offensive
core_image: 麻袋布面上扎手的一根根粗纤维
scene: 麻袋的布面扎手，纤维一根根粗得看得清。 The sack was made of coarse cloth that scratched his hands.
sceneCN: 这里 coarse 指「粗糙的」（第 1 个义项：手感不光滑）；句意是这只麻袋用粗糙的布做成，扎他的手。

derivatives.zh: 粗糙地；粗鲁地
粗糙；粗俗
使变粗糙；使变粗俗

senses.title: Rough to the touch
senses.definition: made of thick threads or fibres and not smooth to touch
senses.definitionCN: 由粗线或粗纤维制成、摸起来不光滑
senses.example: The sack was made of coarse cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这只麻袋是用粗布做的。
senses.why: The word began as a spelling of course, meaning plain and ordinary, and plain cloth is often rough.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本是 course 的另一种拼法，意为平常普通，而普通的布往往粗糙。

senses.title: Rude and offensive
senses.definition: using words or behaving in a way that offends people
senses.definitionCN: 用词或举止令人反感
senses.example: His coarse jokes embarrassed the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗俗的玩笑让客人尴尬。
senses.why: Rough cloth and rough speech share the idea of something unrefined.
senses.whyCN: 粗糙的布与粗鲁的言语共享「未经打磨」这一意思。

senses.title: Made of large particles
senses.definition: consisting of relatively large pieces or grains
senses.definitionCN: 由相对较大的块或颗粒组成
senses.example: Coarse sand drains faster than fine sand.
senses.exampleCN: 粗砂比细砂排水快。
senses.why: A grain that is not ground fine looks rough under the fingers, so the texture word covers size too.
senses.whyCN: 没有磨细的颗粒摸起来粗糙，于是质地词也涵盖了颗粒大小。

intro.en: Coarse is a later spelling of course, and the two words split only in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: coarse 是 course 的后起拼法，两词到十八世纪才分开。

items.en: Cursus meant a running or a set path.
items.cn: cursus 指奔跑或固定的路径。

items.en: Cours meant ordinary, plain or of the usual kind.
items.cn: cours 意为普通的、平常的。

items.en: Course could describe plain everyday cloth.
items.cn: course 可以形容日常的普通布料。

items.en: Coarse was fixed as a separate spelling for rough things.
items.cn: coarse 被固定为表示粗糙之物的独立拼法。

items.en: The word now also means rude and large-grained.
items.cn: 这个词如今还指粗鲁与颗粒粗大。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound the same but differ in spelling, while the meaning group names roughness.
note.cn: 形近组收同音但拼写不同的词，近义组列出粗糙与粗野。

entries.definition: a series of lessons or the direction of travel
entries.definitionCN: 一系列课程，或行进的方向

entries.definition: having a rough voice because of a sore throat
entries.definitionCN: 因喉咙痛而声音沙哑的

entries.definition: in a rough or rude manner
not smooth or even on the surface
simple and without skill or fine detail
entries.definitionCN: 简单而缺少技巧或细节的

entries.definition: offensive in a way that shows bad manners
entries.definitionCN: 以失礼方式令人反感的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the identical sound with course, the rough sack and the large grains.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从与 course 同音、扎手的麻袋和粗大颗粒入手。

normal.en: Coarse and course sound the same; the shorter spelling belongs to rough things.
normal.cn: coarse 与 course 同音，拼写较短的那个指粗糙之物。

normal.en: Coarse cloth is cloth that has not been smoothed.
normal.cn: coarse cloth 就是没有弄光滑的布。

normal.en: Coarse sand leaves the fingers feeling the grains.
normal.cn: 粗砂让手指摸得到一颗颗砂粒。

normal.en: Coarse jokes are jokes that rub the wrong way.
normal.cn: coarse jokes 就是逆着人来的玩笑。

normal.en: Coarsen adds -en and makes the adjective into a verb.
normal.cn: coarsen 加 -en，把形容词变成动词。

abstract.en: Picture a burlap sack with thick brown threads.
abstract.cn: 想象一只麻袋，棕色粗线清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of sand that falls in heavy grains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把沉甸甸落下的大颗砂子。

abstract.en: Picture a voice at the next table that is too loud and too rude.
abstract.cn: 想象邻桌那把又响又无礼的嗓子。

examples.en: The path was covered with coarse sand.
examples.cn: 小路上铺着粗砂。

examples.en: A coarse towel felt harsh against his skin.
examples.cn: 粗毛巾擦在皮肤上有些扎。

examples.en: She never used coarse words in front of children.
examples.cn: 她从不在孩子面前说粗话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 coarse 记成「没磨过的东西」：布没磨光就扎手，话没磨过就扎耳。

root: 由 course（普通的、平常的）分化出的拼写，十八世纪固定为表示粗糙、粗俗的独立词。

sensesIntro.en: From plain ordinary cloth to rough texture, then to large grains and rude behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 从普通的布，到粗糙的质地，再到粗大的颗粒与粗鲁的举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that has never been smoothed.
core.cn: 核心意象：从未被打磨光滑的表面。

branches.en: The texture sense is the most physical branch.
branches.cn: 质地义是最具体的一支。

branches.en: Rude words are treated as an unrefined surface.
branches.cn: 粗鲁的话语被当作未经打磨的表面。

branches.en: Large grains show the same refusal to be fine.
branches.cn: 粗大颗粒同样表现出不细。

branches.en: Texture and grain size are two readings of the same surface.
branches.cn: 质地与颗粒大小是同一表面的两种读法。

branches.en: Rough cloth and rough manners share one judgement.
branches.cn: 粗布与粗鲁举止共享同一种评价。

intro.en: The stem takes comparison forms, an adverb, a noun and a verb, plus texture compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词干长出比较级、副词、名词与动词，并构成质地类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin cursus, a course, through French cours, meaning ordinary.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 cursus（行程），经法语 cours（普通的）而来。

items.example: This paper is coarser than the other.
items.exampleCN: 这种纸比另一种更粗糙。

items.example: The coarseness of the fabric kept him warm.
items.exampleCN: 织物的粗糙反倒让他暖和。

items.example: The rock is coarse-grained and grey.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石颗粒粗大，呈灰色。

items.example: The wall has a coarse-textured finish.
items.exampleCN: 墙面有一层粗糙的涂层。
那个说话粗鲁的人后来道了歉。

latinEntries.meaning: a running or a set course
latinEntries.exampleCN: cursus 在法语中成为 cours。

definition_en: a person who lives by asking for money or food
core_image: 寒风里缩在墙角的一个破旧身影
scene: 街角的石阶上坐着一个人。 A beggar held out an empty bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 beggar 是「乞丐」（第 1 个义项：靠乞讨为生的人）；句意是一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。

pos.zh: 动词：使贫穷；使难以描述

derivatives.zh: 由 beggar 加 -ly 构成，义为「贫穷的」
由 beggar 加 -y 构成，义为「乞讨；极度贫穷」
beggar 的基础动词，义为「乞讨」

senses.title: A person who begs
senses.definition: a person who lives by asking others for money or food
senses.definitionCN: 靠向他人讨钱或讨食为生的人
senses.example: A beggar held out an empty bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。
senses.why: The word came from an old French name for a member of a begging order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语中称呼乞讨教团成员的名称。

senses.title: To make poor or beyond words
senses.definition: to make someone poor, or to be too strange to describe
senses.definitionCN: 使某人贫穷，或奇特得无法描述
senses.example: The war beggared the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 战争使整个地区陷入贫困。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to reduce to beggary.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示使人沦为乞丐般的贫穷。

intro.en: Beggar first named a member of a religious begging order.
intro.cn: beggar 最初指某个以乞讨为生的宗教教团成员。

items.en: begard named a member of a begging order.
items.cn: begard 指乞讨教团的成员。

items.en: begger meant a person who begs.
items.cn: begger 指乞讨的人。

items.en: beggar became the usual spelling.
items.cn: beggar 成为常见拼写。

items.en: the noun also became a verb.
items.cn: 名词又转为动词。

items.en: beggar belief means too strange to believe.
items.cn: 如今 beggar belief 指难以置信。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives other poor or homeless words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是其他表示贫穷或流浪的词。

normalIntro.en: A beggar asks for money, and to beggar is to make poor.
normalIntro.cn: beggar 是讨钱的人，作动词则指使人贫穷。

normal.en: The plural is beggars.
normal.cn: 复数是 beggars。

normal.en: Beg is the short verb behind it.

normal.en: Beggar belief means too strange to believe.
normal.cn: beggar belief 指难以置信。

normal.en: Beggary means great poverty.
normal.cn: beggary 指极度贫穷。

abstract.en: See a ruined town after war.

examples.cn: 一个乞丐伸出一只空碗。

examples.cn: 战争使整个地区陷入贫困。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beggar 想成墙角那只伸出来的空碗。

definition_zh: 插入；嵌入；（在文字中）添加
definition_en: to put something inside or between other things, or to add words to a text
core_image: 一枚硬币被手指推进投币口的窄缝里
scene: 打印机卡纸了，说明书上有一行加粗的提示。 Insert the card face up and wait for the light to turn green.
sceneCN: 这里 insert 是「插入」（第 1 个义项：把东西放进或放进两物之间）；句意为正面朝上插入卡片，等指示灯变绿。图中可辨识物件：卡片、插槽、指示灯。

pos.zh: 动词：插入；嵌入；添加（文字）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「插入；插入物」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「可插入的」
由本词加前缀构成，义为「重新插入」

senses.title: To put inside
senses.definition: to put something carefully inside something else or between two things
senses.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放进另一物之内或两物之间
senses.example: Insert the plug into the socket.
senses.exampleCN: 把插头插入插座。
senses.why: In- "into" plus serere "to join, weave" gives "to join in": something is threaded into a place already filled.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 serere「连接、编织」，意为「编进去」：把东西穿进已经占满的位置。

senses.title: To add words to a text
senses.definition: to add a word, sentence, or paragraph to a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 在文章中增添词语、句子或段落
senses.example: Insert a comma after the first clause.
senses.exampleCN: 在第一个从句后加一个逗号。
senses.why: Text has its own gaps, so an insertion is a piece of writing threaded into the existing line.
senses.whyCN: 文字有它自己的空隙，所以插入就是一段文字被编进已有的行里。

senses.title: Something put in
senses.definition: a loose sheet, picture, or object placed inside something else
senses.definitionCN: 放在其他东西里面的散页、图片或物件
senses.example: The magazine came with a colour insert.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志附有一张彩色插页。
senses.why: The noun uses the same form and names the very thing that was threaded in.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式相同，指的就是被编进去的那件东西。

intro.en: Insert comes from a Latin verb of joining or weaving in, which is why it suggests careful threading rather than pushing.
intro.cn: insert 来自拉丁语表示「编入、接入」的动词，因此它暗示的是细心穿入而非硬塞。

items.en: Serere meant "to join, bind, weave", the root of series and sermon.
items.cn: serere 意为「连接、编织」，是 series 与 sermon 的词根。

items.en: Inserere, from in- plus serere, meant "to graft or insert, to weave into".
items.cn: inserere 由 in- 加 serere 构成，意为「嫁接、插入、编入」。

items.en: The noun insertio was used for grafting plants and for joining words.
items.cn: 名词 insertio 用于植物嫁接，也用于词语接入。

items.en: English borrowed insert in the sixteenth century for both planting and writing.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 insert，兼用于种植与文字。

items.en: Modern use centres on cards, plugs, and paragraphs added to texts.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在卡片、插头以及插入正文的段落。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of joining; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting something inside.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「连接」动词；近义组收把东西放进里面的动词。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in, or the thing put in.
A number of things joined in order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「系列」，即依次连接之物。

entries.definition: To state something firmly, with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断言」，形近但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for placing something inside.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「放入」，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To join something to a group or a text without the idea of a tight fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「添加」，不含紧贴嵌入之意。

entries.definition: To fix something firmly into living tissue or a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「植入」，多指植入活体组织或观念。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use serere, the verb of weaving, and the phrases insert appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「编织」动词 serere，以及 insert 的搭配。

normal.en: Serere is to weave: to insert is to thread something into a place.
normal.cn: serere 是「编织」：insert 就是把东西穿进某个位置。

normal.en: Insert takes a direct object: insert a card, insert a comma.
normal.cn: insert 直接带宾语：insert a card、insert a comma。

normal.en: Insert into is the form used with a container.
normal.cn: 与容器连用时用 insert into。

normal.en: Insertion is the noun; reinsert means to do it again.
normal.cn: 名词是 insertion；reinsert 表示重新插入。

normal.en: A colour insert falls out of the magazine.
normal.cn: 彩色插页从杂志里掉出来。

abstract.en: Picture threading a needle: the fit must be exact, not forced.
abstract.cn: 想象穿针引线：要严丝合缝，不能硬塞。

abstract.en: To insert is to interrupt a line without breaking it.
abstract.cn: 插入是在不打乱整体的前提下在中间加入。

abstract.en: Writers insert clauses the way joiners fit new pieces of wood.
abstract.cn: 作者插入从句，正如木匠嵌入新的木料。

examples.en: Insert your ticket into the machine.
examples.cn: 把车票插入机器。

examples.en: She inserted a new line into the report.
examples.cn: 她在报告里加了一行。

examples.en: The book has an eight-page photographic insert.
examples.cn: 这本书有八页的摄影插页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因瑟特」——因要把卡片「瑟」进缝里，便是插入

root: 拉丁语 serere「连接、编织」加 in-「向内」构成 inserere「编入、插入」，名词 insertio 用于嫁接与文字；英语十六世纪借入 insert。同根词有 insertion、series。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting an object in, adding words to a text, and the thing that is put in.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：放入物体、在文字中添加，以及被放进去的东西本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin is pushed into the narrow slot of a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币被推进机器的窄缝。

branches.en: THE SLOT: cards and plugs are inserted into narrow openings.
branches.cn: 插槽这条线：卡片与插头被插进狭窄的开口。

branches.en: THE GRAFT: gardening uses the same verb for joining a shoot to a stem.
branches.cn: 嫁接这条线：园艺用同一个动词表示把枝条接到树干上。

branches.en: THE PAGE: writers insert clauses and commas into a finished line.
branches.cn: 纸页这条线：作者把从句与逗号插入已有的行里。

branches.en: THE MAGAZINE: an insert is a loose sheet placed inside.
branches.cn: 杂志这条线：insert 指夹在里面的散页。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense describes something entering an existing order without replacing it.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都在描述某物进入既有秩序而不替代它。

intro.en: Insert is a Latin prefix on a weaving root, with an English verb ending preserved from Latin.
intro.cn: insert 是拉丁语前缀加「编织」词根，动词词尾沿用拉丁语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin serere, inserere and insertio are recorded, along with series and sertum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serere、inserere、insertio 均有记录，还有 series 与 sertum。

items.example: It marks the direction of joining.
It shows in insert and insert usages.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 insert 相关形式中。

items.example: The direct source of the verb.
A cousin from the same root.
Another form made from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 这是由同一词干构成的另一形式。

definition_zh: 解放；使获得自由；释放；解除束缚
definition_en: to set a person or place free from control, or to release something that was held back
core_image: 牢门上的铁锁被剪断，门向外推开，光落到台阶上
scene: 城门在清晨被推开，围在广场上的人群让出一条路，被关押多年的人慢慢走出来。 The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里是「解放」（第 1 个义项：使一个地方脱离控制）；句意为士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。图中可辨识物件：推开的城门、让路的人群、石阶上的光。

pos.zh: 解放；使获得自由；释放；解除束缚

derivatives.zh: 由 liberate 去 e 加 -ion 构成，义为「解放；释放」
由 liberate 加 -or 构成，义为「解放者」
由现在分词转成的形容词，义为「令人感到解脱的」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已获解放的；思想开放的」

senses.title: To free a place or its people from outside control
senses.definition: to drive an occupying power or an oppressive force out of a place and its people
senses.definitionCN: 把占领者或压迫性力量从一个地方及其人民身上赶走
senses.example: The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。
senses.why: Latin liber meant free, and the verb liberare made that state happen; the object here is a whole community, so the word names a collective act of freeing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liber 意为自由的，动词 liberare 就是让这种状态发生；这里的对象是整个群体，所以这个词指的是一次集体的解救行动。

senses.title: To set a prisoner or captive free
senses.definition: to open the way out for a person held in prison or captivity
senses.definitionCN: 为被关押或囚禁的人打开出去的路
senses.example: The rebels liberated every prisoner in the jail.
senses.exampleCN: 起义者把监狱里的囚犯全部释放了。
senses.why: The same verb turns from a town to a single body behind bars; freedom is now measured by a door that opens for one person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从一座城转到铁栏后的一个身体；此时的自由，衡量的就是有一扇门为这一个人打开。

senses.title: To free someone from something that limits them
senses.definition: to free a person from a habit, fear or narrow way of thinking that holds them back
senses.definitionCN: 使人从阻碍自己的习惯、恐惧或狭隘想法中脱身
senses.example: Travel liberated her from a narrow view of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行把她从狭隘的世界观里解放出来。
senses.why: Here the prison is invisible: what holds a person is a habit or an idea, and the verb works by loosening that grip rather than by breaking a lock.
senses.whyCN: 这里的牢笼看不见：困住一个人的是习惯或观念，动词的作用是松开这只手，而不是砸开一把锁。

senses.title: To release something stored or bound
senses.definition: to set loose a gas, heat or energy that was held in a substance or a system
senses.definitionCN: 把原本束缚在某种物质或系统中的气体、热量或能量放出来
senses.example: The reaction liberates heat and light.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应释放出热和光。
senses.why: Chemistry keeps the oldest image in plain sight: what was bound inside a compound is let go, exactly as a prisoner is let out of a cell.
senses.whyCN: 化学把最古老的画面摆得明明白白：原本被束缚在化合物里的东西被放开，就像囚犯被放出牢房。

intro.en: Liberate is built from a Latin adjective for free plus a verb ending, and its family has carried the idea of freedom through law, politics and chemistry.
intro.cn: liberate 由拉丁语中表示「自由」的形容词加动词词尾构成，这一族词把「自由」的观念从法律带到政治，再带到化学。

items.en: Liber was an adjective meaning free, and as a noun it named a free person as opposed to a slave.
items.cn: liber 是表示「自由的」形容词，作名词时指自由人，与奴隶相对。

items.en: Liberare meant to set free or to release, and it became the verb English borrowed.
items.cn: liberare 意为使自由、释放，正是英语借走的那个动词。

items.en: Libertas was the abstract noun for freedom, the state that the verb produced.
items.cn: libertas 是表示「自由」的抽象名词，即那个动词所造成的状态。

items.en: Old French liberer passed the verb on, first used in legal and religious settings.
items.cn: 古法语 liberer 把这个动词传下来，最早用于法律与宗教场合。

items.en: Modern English keeps liberate for freeing peoples, prisoners, minds and substances, while liberty and liberal carry the noun and adjective side.
items.cn: 现代英语用 liberate 表示解放民族、囚犯、心灵与物质，而 liberty 与 liberal 承担名词与形容词的一面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the Latin free root; the near-meaning group collects verbs of letting someone go.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「自由」词根上的同族词；近义组收表示「放人走」的动词。

entries.definition: The state of being free, the noun built beside the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 自由的状态，与动词并列构成的名词。

entries.definition: Open to new ideas or favouring individual freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 思想开放的；主张个人自由的。

entries.definition: The act of setting people free.
entries.definitionCN: 把人们释放出来的行为；解放。

entries.definition: To hand something over or to save someone, built on the same free root with a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 送出或解救，在同一词根前加前缀构成。

entries.definition: To let someone go or to remove a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 放某人走，或去掉一项限制。

entries.definition: To let a person or thing go free.
To free someone from legal or social control.
entries.definitionCN: 使摆脱法律或社会控制；解放。

entries.definition: To save someone from danger or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人从危险或伤害中救出。

normalIntro.en: The word is an action made from the Latin adjective for free, and the whole family divides the work between the state, the act and the person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「自由的」形容词造出的动作，整族词把「状态、动作、人」分得清清楚楚。

normal.en: Liber is Latin for free, and the ending -are turns that adjective into the verb to make free.
normal.cn: liber 是拉丁语的「自由的」，词尾 -are 把这个形容词变成动词「使自由」。

normal.en: Liberty names the state, liberate names the act, and liberator names the person who does it.
normal.cn: liberty 指状态，liberate 指动作，liberator 指做这件事的人。

normal.en: Deliver is a prefix plus the same root: to deliver is to let something pass out of one's hands.
normal.cn: deliver 是前缀加同一词根：交出某物，就是让它离开自己的手。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks verbs of making, as in liberate and activate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 常标记「使……发生」的动词，如 liberate 与 activate。

normal.en: Chemists say a reaction liberates a gas when the gas is set loose from a compound.
normal.cn: 化学里说某反应 liberates 一种气体，就是那种气体从化合物中被放了出来。

abstract.en: The word always has a door in it: something closed is made open.
abstract.cn: 这个词里始终有一扇门：原本关着的被打开了。

abstract.en: Freedom here is described as an action rather than a possession, which is why a verb stands beside the abstract noun.
abstract.cn: 这里的自由被说成一个动作而不是一件所有物，所以抽象名词旁边还站着一个动词。

abstract.en: To liberate a mind uses the same verb as to liberate a city, as if ideas could be held prisoner too.
abstract.cn: 解放心灵与解放城市用的是同一个动词，仿佛观念也会被关押。

examples.en: The soldiers liberated the town at dawn.
examples.cn: 士兵们在黎明时解放了这座城镇。

examples.en: The rebels liberated every prisoner in the jail.
examples.cn: 起义者把监狱里的囚犯全部释放了。

examples.en: The reaction liberates heat and light.
examples.cn: 这个反应释放出热和光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离吧，解脱了」——离吧，人一走自由就来了；liberate 是解放。

root: 拉丁语 liber（自由的）+ 动词词尾 -are，liberare 意为「使自由、释放」；同族有 liberty、liberal、liberation，前缀变体有 deliver。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person or place being let out of someone else's control; it spreads from a town to a prisoner, then to a mind, and finally to a gas inside a compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个人、一个地方被放出别人的控制；它从一座城扩展到一名囚犯，再扩到一颗心灵，最后扩到化合物里的气体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut padlock falling away as the gate swings outward into the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锁被剪断落下，大门向光里打开。

branches.en: a gate opening for a whole crowd at dawn
branches.cn: 黎明时为一群人打开的大门

branches.en: one cell door standing open with nobody guarding it
branches.cn: 一扇没人看守的牢房门开着

branches.en: a traveller returning with a wider view of the world
branches.cn: 旅行归来、眼界变宽的旅人

branches.en: heat and light leaving a reacting mixture
branches.cn: 热与光从反应物中逸出

branches.en: one verb covering a town and a single body
branches.cn: 一个动词同时覆盖一座城与一个身体

intro.en: A Latin adjective for free, its verb, its abstract noun, and two English endings that mark action, result and person hold the family together.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「自由的」形容词、它的动词、它的抽象名词，以及两个标记动作、结果与人的英语词尾，把这个词族撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: Liber, liberare and libertas are all recorded Latin words, so the family has a reliable Latin core.
latinIntro.cn: liber、liberare 与 libertas 都是有记录的拉丁词，这一族有可靠的拉丁语内核。

definition_zh: 杂草；野草；菸草（口语）；除草
definition_en: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted, and also to remove such plants
core_image: 菜畦里一丛比菜苗还壮的野草，被人一把连根拔起
scene: 雨后的菜畦里，野草长得比菜苗还高，母亲蹲下把它们一株株拔起来。 After the rain the weeds stood taller than the young vegetables, so we pulled them out.
sceneCN: 这里 weed 是「杂草」（第 1 个义项：长在不该长地方的野生植物）；句意为雨后野草比菜苗还高，我们把它拔掉。比菜苗还壮、被连根拔起的那丛草就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 多杂草的；瘦弱的
除草
除草剂
海草；海藻
无杂草的

senses.title: A plant in the wrong place
senses.definition: a wild plant growing where people do not want it
senses.definitionCN: 长在人们不需要的地方的野生植物
senses.example: Dandelions are a weed in a lawn and a flower in a meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 蒲公英在草坪上是杂草，在草甸上是花。
senses.why: This is the core sense, and it depends on place rather than species.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，取决于位置而非种类。

senses.title: To remove such plants
senses.definition: to pull out or cut unwanted plants from a garden or field
senses.definitionCN: 从园圃或田地里拔掉或割掉不受欢迎的植物
senses.example: They weeded the beds before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们到来之前，他们把花坛的草清干净了。
senses.why: Once the noun named the plant, the verb named the work.
senses.whyCN: 名词指草之后，动词就指拔草这件事。

senses.title: To remove unwanted things or people
senses.definition: to get rid of weak or unwanted members from a group
senses.definitionCN: 从群体中清掉弱的或不需要的成员
senses.example: The first round weeds out the weakest entries.
senses.exampleCN: 第一轮会淘汰最弱的参赛作品。
senses.why: Pulling weak plants out of a bed gives the image for clearing a list.
senses.whyCN: 把弱苗从苗床里拔掉，为清理名单提供了意象。

senses.title: Tobacco, in informal use
senses.definition: an old slang word for tobacco or a cigarette
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指菸草或香烟
senses.example: He stepped outside for a weed.
senses.exampleCN: 他走到外面抽支烟。
senses.why: This slang sense is old and has almost disappeared from polite speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一俚语义已陈旧，在正式场合几乎绝迹。

senses.title: A troublesome person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing seen as a nuisance, in slang
senses.definitionCN: 口语中令人讨厌的人或事
senses.example: That old car is a weed of a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车真是台麻烦机器。
senses.why: Something that grows where it is not wanted and will not go away suits both plants and pests.
senses.whyCN: 在不该生长的地方长起来又除不掉的东西，既像草也像麻烦。

intro.en: Weed is an Old English word for a harmful herb, and it once carried the sense of something poisonous or worthless.
intro.cn: weed 是古英语中表示有害草木的词，曾带有「有毒、无用」的意味。

items.en: Wēod meant a herb, especially a harmful one growing among crops.
items.cn: wēod 意为草木，尤指长在作物间的有害草木。

items.en: Related forms in Dutch and German also mean weed, so the sense is very old.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中的相关形式也表示杂草，可见这个意义很古老。

items.en: Spelling settled as weed and the garden sense became fixed.
items.cn: 拼写定为 weed，园艺义随之固定。

items.en: Weed out grew from garden work into any clearing of a group.
items.cn: weed out 从园艺劳动扩展到对任何群体的清理。

items.en: Slang uses for tobacco and for a tiresome person came and mostly went.
items.cn: 指菸草与讨厌之人的俚语用法出现过，又多半消散。

note.en: The first group shares the weed word, the second names plants and clearing work.
note.cn: 第一组与 weed 同词同源，第二组指植物与清理工作。

entries.definition: Full of weeds, or thin and weak.
Plant-like growth in the sea.
A substance that kills weeds.
The work of removing weeds.
The common green ground plant, wanted on lawns.
Any living green thing that grows in soil.
A plant used for food or medicine.
Loosening soil and cutting weeds with a hoe.

normalIntro.en: A weed is not a kind of plant but a plant in the wrong place, which is why the verb can also mean to clear a list.
normalIntro.cn: 杂草不是某个种类，而是长错地方的植物，所以动词也能表示清理名单。

normal.en: Weed is both the plant and the pulling of it.
normal.cn: weed 既是草，也是拔草。

normal.en: Weed out means remove the weak ones.
normal.cn: weed out 意为剔除弱者。

normal.en: Weedy grounds are full of weeds; a weedy person is thin.
normal.cn: weedy 地面满是草，weedy 的人很瘦。

normal.en: Seaweed is not a garden pest at all.
normal.cn: seaweed 根本不是园中害虫。

normal.en: Weedkiller is what stops you weeding by hand.
normal.cn: weedkiller 让你不必动手拔草。

abstract.en: Picture a thistle standing higher than lettuce.
abstract.cn: 想一株飞蓟比生菜还高。

abstract.en: Feel the root come free with a quick tug.

definition_zh: 绝望；灰心；对……不再抱有希望
definition_en: a feeling that there is no hope at all
core_image: 一个人坐在熄了灯的房间地板上，背靠着门
scene: 连续几次面试都没有回音，他把简历扣在桌上不再去看。 After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
sceneCN: 这里 despair 指「绝望」（第 1 个义项：完全看不到希望的感受）；句意是几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。

derivatives.zh: 绝望的

senses.title: No hope left at all
senses.definition: the feeling that there is no hope and nothing can be done
senses.definitionCN: 觉得毫无希望、无事可做的感受
senses.example: After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
senses.exampleCN: 几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。
senses.why: Despair is hope with the future switched off.
senses.whyCN: 绝望就是把未来的开关关掉之后的希望。

senses.title: Stop hoping for it
senses.definition: to stop hoping that something will happen or improve
senses.definitionCN: 不再希望某事发生或好转
senses.example: He despaired of ever finding a job in that town.
senses.exampleCN: 他对在那个镇上找到工作已不抱希望。
senses.why: The noun's feeling turns into a verb the moment it is aimed at one thing.
senses.whyCN: 当这种感受对准一件具体的事，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: The thing that defeats hope
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes other people feel hopeless
senses.definitionCN: 使别人感到毫无希望的人或事物
senses.example: The tangled wires were the despair of every repairman.
senses.exampleCN: 那团乱线是每个修理工的噩梦。
senses.why: Something so bad it defeats everyone ends up wearing the feeling it causes.
senses.whyCN: 糟糕到让所有人败下阵来的东西，最后会戴上它造成的感受。

intro.en: Despair comes from Latin desperare, to lose hope, built on de-, away, and sperare, to hope, from spes, hope.
intro.cn: despair 来自拉丁语 desperare（失去希望），由 de-（离开）与 sperare（希望）构成，后者源于 spes（希望）。

items.en: Spes was hope, and sperare meant to hope for something.
items.cn: spes 是希望，sperare 指对某事抱着希望。

items.en: De- reversed the verb, so desperare meant to hope no longer.
items.cn: de- 把这个动词反过来，desperare 就是不再抱有希望。

items.en: Desesperer kept the whole weight of the lost hope.
items.cn: desesperer 完整保留了失去希望的沉重感。

items.en: English used it as both a noun of feeling and a verb of giving up.
items.cn: 英语把它同时用作表示感受的名词与表示放弃的动词。

items.en: It can now even name a thing that defeats everyone who deals with it.
items.cn: 如今它甚至能指一件让所有接触者都束手无策的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sper root of hope, and the meaning group all sit close to hopelessness.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示希望的 sper 词基，近义组则都挨着「无望」这一带。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a back against a closed door and end with a tangle of wires nobody can fix.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从背靠一扇关着的门开始，落到一团谁也理不清的乱线。

normal.en: Despair is hope that has stopped answering the door.
normal.cn: 绝望是希望不再来应门。

normal.en: De- takes the hope away and leaves the room empty.
normal.cn: de- 把希望拿走，房间就空了。

normal.en: The same word can be a feeling, an act and a thing.
normal.cn: 同一个词，可以是感受、是动作，也可以是一件东西。

normal.en: To despair of a town is to stop looking down its streets.
normal.cn: 对一座镇子绝望，就是不再朝它的街上张望。

normal.en: Some tasks are called the despair of workers because they beat everyone.
normal.cn: 有些活儿被叫作工人的噩梦，因为它们把每个人打败。

abstract.en: Picture a row of unopened letters on a dark table.
abstract.cn: 想象暗桌上摆着一排没拆的信。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that reaches for the phone and then stops.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向电话，又停住了。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the bulb has quietly gone out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，灯泡悄悄熄了。

examples.en: After months of failed attempts, he sank into despair.
examples.cn: 几个月尝试失败后，他陷入了绝望。

examples.en: He despaired of ever finding a job in that town.
examples.cn: 他对在那个镇上找到工作已不抱希望。

examples.en: She looked at the broken machine in despair.
examples.cn: 她绝望地看着那台坏掉的机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 despair 记成「地死背儿」：de 是去掉，spair 像「希望」，希望被拿掉，只剩绝望。

root: 来自拉丁语 desperare（失去希望），由 de-（离开）与 sperare（希望）构成，sperare 又源于 spes（希望）。本义是把希望放走，后来指彻底看不到出路的感受，也可作动词表示不再指望，还指把人逼到无路可走的事物。

sensesIntro.en: From a feeling with no future, to the act of giving up on one thing, to a thing that makes everyone give up.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有未来的感受，到对某件事放弃期待的动作，再到让所有人都放弃的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where the last lamp goes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮着的屋子，最后一盏灯灭了。

branches.en: The first sense is the darkness filling the whole room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是黑暗填满整个房间。

branches.en: The second sense aims that darkness at one closed door.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把那片黑暗对准一扇关上的门。

branches.en: The third sense lets a thing carry the darkness for others.
branches.cn: 第三个义项让一件东西替别人背着那片黑暗。

branches.en: A mood and a decision differ only in how wide they reach.
branches.cn: 一种心境与一个决定，差别只在于波及多宽。

branches.en: What defeats many people becomes a byword for the feeling.
branches.cn: 让许多人败下阵来的东西，成了这种感受的代名词。

intro.en: Despair belongs to a Latin family built on hope, and its relatives spread from the feeling to the reckless act.
intro.cn: despair 属于一族建在「希望」上的拉丁词，同族词从这种感受延伸到不顾一切的行动。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin spes, hope; de- removes it, and the family keeps the same root in desperate and desperation.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 spes（希望），前缀 de- 把它拿走，desperate 与 desperation 沿用同一词根。
